description: Gating backfill program (81-band). A quality pass over the checksets the backfill generates: audit them for fabricated or trivial questions and tighten checkset_failures so backfilled gates hold the SAME bar as hand-built ones, keeping verify_code=True the load-bearing check (a code check's reference `solution` run against its own `test` in a subprocess before the set may be written). This is the gating-side analogue of construct.py's construction_failures discipline: tighten THIS grader when a new fabrication is found, keep its sentences specific (they are the repair prompt and the UI's error text). The risk backfill-at-scale introduces is a checkset that technically validates but asks nothing real — a choice question whose answer is given away, a short question the rubric already answers, a code check whose test asserts nothing meaningful — and this band is the guard against it. Depends on the batched-gating story (79), whose output it audits. Anti-fabrication IS the deliverable: a fabricated or trivial checkset is rejected by the tightened checkset_failures and never written, and a test proves a deliberately trivial/fabricated set is caught while a genuine one passes.
warmup: echo '--- the grader to tighten, and its load-bearing verify_code half ---'; sed -n '362,420p' praxis/checks.py
echo '--- the sibling discipline on the construction side ---'; grep -n 'def construction_failures\|def gate_failures\|fabricat' praxis/rubric.py | head
echo '--- the rule that carries the weight: solution run against its own test ---'; grep -n 'verify_code\|subprocess\|solution\|def _run' praxis/checks.py | head

userStories.title: Audit backfilled checksets for fabricated or trivial questions
acceptanceCriteria: An audit pass scans the checksets produced by the 79 backfill for the failure modes scale introduces — an answer given away in the prompt, a short-answer the notebook body already answers verbatim, a code check whose test asserts nothing, a duplicated/near-identical question across sections — and reports each with a specific reason.

The audit reuses the shipped signals (checkset_failures shape, the GATED_SECTIONS coverage, the verify_code subprocess result) rather than a parallel grader, so it measures the same thing the write path enforces.
Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that the audit flags a deliberately trivial/fabricated fixture checkset and passes a genuine one.

userStories.title: Tighten checkset_failures so a trivial set can never be written
acceptanceCriteria: checkset_failures is tightened so the fabrication/triviality modes the audit found are caught at write time — a set exhibiting one is rejected and never written (same rule as the constructor), with verify_code=True kept as the load-bearing check that a code check's solution really runs against its own test.

The new failure sentences are specific enough to act on (they feed the repair prompt and surface as the UI's error text), and the cheap load path (needs_checks / verify_code=False) stays cheap — the tightening lands only on the write/verify path.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers the tightened rules — asserting a fabricated/trivial set is rejected with an actionable message and that the existing hand-built seed checksets still pass (no regression to the 24 already gated).

userStories.title: Re-audit checksets written before the tightened bar, and regenerate only by policy
acceptanceCriteria: A re-audit pass runs the tightened checkset_failures over every checkset already on disk that was written BEFORE the tightening landed (79 batches may run before this band merges), reporting each set that no longer meets the bar with the grader's specific sentence — measuring with the same tightened write-path grader, never a parallel one.

The gate rules are respected: an already-gated notebook's checkset is skipped, not rewritten — a pre-tightening set that now fails is FLAGGED for regeneration, and regeneration is an explicit per-notebook pass through the shipped checks.py write path (grade-then-write, verify_code=True), so a regenerated set that fails the tightened bar is never written and the existing set stays in place rather than leaving the notebook ungated.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that the re-audit flags a fixture checkset failing only the NEW rules while leaving it on disk untouched, and that an explicit regeneration replaces it only with a set passing the tightened bar.
